newsitem.title: UK: Severn Trent plans to complete share buyback.
newsitem.headline: Severn Trent plans to complete share buyback.

text.p: British water and sewerage company Severn Trent Plc said on Tuesday that it planned to complete a buyback of shares announced last year if approved by its annual meeting.

Severn Trent, which said last year that it would buy back up to 10 percent of its shares and bought 5.6 percent during December 1996, announced pretax profits for the year of 391 million pounds ($639.3 million), within expectations, and paid out a total dividend of 36.5 pence per share, up 12.8 percent.

The company said it had made a 20 million pounds provision to complete cover for a 29 million pound reorganisation of its water and sewerage business which should see cost savings starting from 1997/98 rising to 12 million pounds per year by 2000/01.

"The group has made highly satisfactory progress this year with excellent results from both the regulated water utility and the non-regulated companies, which now account for 30 percent of total turnover," Severn Trent said in a statement.

The company said future strategy would focus on building a world class water services organisation, looking for opportunities for profitable growth in the waste industry and expanding its presence in selected markets for utility related services.

Severn Trent said its confidence in the future was qualified only by continuing uncertainties over proposed changes in the tax and regulatory regimes, as the new Labour government has vowed to introduce a one-off tax on the excess profits of privatised utilities in its first budget on July 2.
